note: The one note that sets Mixolydian apart from major: heard first in a two-scales play-along over the drone (the switch shows as the changed note), then found in two positions with {{1}} and {{b7}} ringed, the last over a drone. The key is now moves (any key), named only as {{=key}}; the play-along's backing chord is gone so the drone follows the key, the note names are degrees, and the last line says what stays the same in another key.

exercise.title: {{=key}} Mixolydian: find the ♭7
exercise.why: Mixolydian is the major scale with one note lowered, the 7th, so that one note is where the mode can be heard: find it first, then aim for it.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track: a drone on {{=key}}, with four bars of the {{=key}} major scale and then four bars of {{=key}} Mixolydian. Play each scale along with the neck, from the lowest note up to the highest and back down.
Listen for the bar where one note changes: the faded note is the one to leave out, {{b7}} in the major half and {{7}} in the Mixolydian half.

cells.heading: Root on the low E string

cells.text:
The note that changed is {{b7}}. Below is the neck with the position of {{=key}} Mixolydian that has {{1}} on the low E string: each dot is a note to play, and {{1}} and {{b7}} are ringed. Tap a ringed {{b7}} to hear it.
Start on {{1}} on the low E string, play up to the high e string and back down, then make up short phrases that stop on {{b7}} and step up to {{1}}.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. Under it is the same mode in the position with {{1}} on the A string. Hold each ringed {{b7}} against the drone, then let it step up to {{1}}.
The goal of this practice is to find {{b7}} from any {{1}} without looking at the neck.
{{?key}}In another key the positions sit on other frets, and {{b7}} is still the note two frets under each {{1}} on the same string.
